description:
`apply_bulk_update` opens sessions only for matched issues that actually need a change, matching the session-budget guarantee already tested for automatic transitions.

## Background

`apply_bulk_update` (`crates/jit/src/commands/bulk_update.rs`) opens a preflight session and a publication session for every filter-matched issue before knowing whether anything changes - cost 2*|matched|. The automatic-transitions path already demonstrates the correct shape: a cheap in-memory eligibility prefilter that can only skip, never authorize, plus an authoritative recheck inside the session.

Add a pure `UpdateOperations::is_provable_noop(&Issue) -> bool` candidate predicate over the already-listed issues. It is Issue-local and no-op-only: it nominates an issue as a skip candidate exactly when every operation's target value already holds (state equal, labels present or absent, priority, gate and assignee state), all decidable from the listed `Issue` alone. Potentially invalid updates are not prefiltered - they still open sessions so the same authoritative in-session validation produces the same per-issue error results as before; repository-dependent validity never moves out of a session, and the prefilter only nominates skips, never authorizes them.

Because the in-session write path evaluates local rules against the projected issue even when no field changes, a field-level no-op on an issue with a pre-existing enforced-rule violation must still produce its pre-change result (an error without `--force`, a logged bypass event with it). Skip candidates therefore receive their authoritative confirmation inside one shared verification session: it captures the repository declarations and the candidate issues, re-verifies field-level no-op-ness and rule cleanliness from that captured state, confirms clean candidates as skipped, and demotes any failing candidate to the normal per-issue session path so its error result is byte-identical to pre-change behavior.

The session-open bound is C*|matched issues that are not confirmed no-ops| plus one shared verification session when at least one skip candidate exists, where C is the per-mutation session constant (currently 2: preflight plus publication). The budget test derives C from a single-issue baseline run rather than hardcoding it, counts session opens via the existing once-per-session-open failure-point probe, seeds K matched issues of which K-J already hold their target values, and asserts C*J + 1 session opens (and exactly C*J when no candidate exists).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `apply_bulk_update` opens per-issue sessions only for matched issues that are not confirmed no-ops; for K matched issues of which J require a change and K-J are confirmed clean no-ops, session opens equal C*J plus one shared verification session (C*J exactly when K-J = 0), where C is the per-mutation session constant.
- [hard] REQ-02: `UpdateOperations::is_provable_noop` is a pure, Issue-local predicate that nominates an issue as a skip candidate exactly when every operation's target value already holds; it never authorizes a skip by itself, and repository-dependent validity is only ever read inside a session (the shared verification session or a per-issue session).
- [hard] REQ-03: An issue whose update is potentially invalid - including a field-level no-op whose projected issue fails rule validation - still reaches a per-issue session and yields the same per-issue error result (and the same `--force` bypass event) as before the change.
- [hard] REQ-04: The session-budget test derives C from a single-issue baseline run, counts session opens via the existing once-per-session-open failure-point probe, seeds K matched issues with K-J already at their target values, and asserts C*J + 1 session opens, plus a zero-candidate case asserting exactly C*J.

## Decisions

- D-1: Skip candidates are confirmed in one shared verification session rather than by a non-session preview read or a purely Issue-local skip. Decided by the invoker on 2026-07-24 after code review found the preview-gated skip could suppress in-session error results; the C*J budget in the original criteria is amended to C*J + 1 to fund the verification session. The per-issue error contract and in-session validation authority take precedence over the exact original budget formula.

## Notes

The change is behavior-preserving for update results: only the number of sessions opened for confirmed no-ops changes. Do not hardcode C; a single-issue baseline run yields it. Recording a bulk-mutation scenario in the benchmark harness is separate work.
title: Bulk-update eligibility prefilter and session budget
